set_aside.subject: PortalStore.begin schema creation ownership
set_aside.text: “the sqlite unit-of-work backend lowers `PortalStore.begin` with them … so no generated module calls them” contradicts State 3’s “`portal_store` owns … schema creation through the repositories” and this flow’s statement that every transaction begins by calling the ten schema functions
set_aside.question: When `PortalStore.begin` creates missing tables, does the generated `portal_store` module invoke the repository schema capabilities, or does a non-module backend perform those calls so that no generated module invokes them?
options: `portal_store` calls the ten repository schema functions in accessor order
The sqlite backend performs schema creation outside every generated module
The backend generates calls inside `portal_store`, and “no generated module calls them” means only that no explicit operation note calls them
set_aside.default_guess: Treat the backend lowering as implementation of `portal_store`: generated `portal_store` code invokes the repository schema functions in accessor order, while routes and use-case notes do not.

witness.initial: The SQLite database exists but contains none of the portal tables.
events: The missing schemas must be created before readiness can complete.
outcomes: Following State 3, generated `module:portal_store` calls each repository’s schema function in accessor order; instrumentation of those module capabilities observes ten calls.
Following the changed State 4 sentence literally, the sqlite backend creates the schemas without any generated module calling those capabilities; the same instrumentation observes no calls.
witness.observer: A later implementer or verification check instrumenting the repository schema capabilities sees the difference.
